log: THE CELL AS A PARTS LIST -- function -> reaction -> parts -> gene -> product -> transport
This enumerates. It does not predict. Every link reports COVERAGE, and absent layers are named
[3] PARTS -- every participant across every reaction, by what it IS
-> NON-PROTEIN share of all participants: 79.6%  (the half a gene-centric view cannot see)
[8] TRANSPORT -- steps whose input and output compartments differ
8,326 of 26,330 reactions cross a compartment boundary (31.6%)
[4,5] MACHINE and GENE -- which reactions have a named catalyst, and is it a gene we know
ORPHAN reactions, no catalyst:  17,551 (61.5%)  <- the biggest hole in the chain
of those, in our gene records:   4,782 (90.5%)
reactions needing >1 gene    :   5,556 (50.6%) -- complexes, i.e. AND logic
[1] FUNCTION -- what the cell has to do, and how much of it has reactions attached
pathway size: median 19, smallest 2 (3-Methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase deficie), largest 2622 (Signal Transduction)
pathways with >=1 gene that catalyses a known reaction: 2,474/2,570 (96.3%)
ABSENT: transcript isoforms / splice variants. The records are GENE-level, so 'which isoform'
cannot be answered from this disk. Needs GENCODE or Ensembl transcript models.
ABSENT: gene biotype, so tRNA / rRNA / snoRNA genes cannot be separated from coding ones here.
ABSENT: no temperature anywhere in these sources. Metabolic models carry compartment pH and
charge at best; Reactome carries neither. Kinetics (kcat/Km) exist only for the enzyme subset
the earlier ecModel work covered, not genome-wide. Reported as a gap, not estimated.
